newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends trading at new six-year low.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends trading at new six-year low.

text.p: The won hit a new six-year closing low on Tuesday as import settlements, buying by the government and dollar short-covering all conspired to pressure the domestic currency, traders said.
The won closed at 836.30, down from the opening high of 834.00. It touched an intra-day low of 836.60.
The closing rate was the lowest level since South Korea started interbank won/dollar trading in 1990, dealers said.
The previous record low was 834.50, set on October 29 this year.
"It's a trend because of the huge current account deficit our country is running," said a Standard Chartered Bank interbank dealer.
"There are more importer settlements coming in than exporter deals, which of course pushes up the dollar," added a Korea First Bank dealer.
The central Bank of Korea has said the current account deficit would reach $22 billion this year, compared with an $8.95 billion shortfall in 1995.

Traders said that players had been cautious at around the 835 level, which had been looked upon as a strong support for the won. But as the level came and went without a peep from the central bank, it became apparent the won was going to weaken further, they said.

"We expect short-covering dolalr selling to emerge even more strongly on Wednesday, which means the dollar is expected to rise again. But we aren't going to take a very long position because we're worried the Bank of Korea will come in," said a European bank dealer. About $300 million worth of buying by the Office of Supply further undermined the won, traders said.
